cards.hook: You chose Dave over Gremly this week. That's not a small thing.

cards.body: Hawaii's weather forced a change of plans, but Bora Bora's stay stretched through Sunday, and the universe seemed to agree with the shift toward presence. A second French Polynesian island awaits the following week. On March 12, the choice became clear: step back from Gremly work and simply be here.
cards.quote: Realizing that even though I love Gremly work, I need to step back sometimes and just enjoy him and being on a once in a lifetime vacation.
cards.headline: Presence won. The honeymoon quietly extended itself.

moments.body: Time on the water with Dave brought a deep physical restoration. The sunburn stung, but it felt like exactly what the body needed—a big dose of vitamin D and presence after weeks of intensity.
moments.title: The Floatie Day

spotlight.title: Productivity without the grind
spotlight.takeaway: You shipped meaningful work while fully present in paradise, then consciously chose to disengage—proving productivity doesn't require constant connection.

research_context.body: Csikszentmihalyi's flow state research shows peak performance emerges when intrinsic motivation aligns with presence, not pressure. Strategic disengagement—what Baumeister calls ego depletion recovery—actually strengthens decision-making and creative output.
